Undertake a range of vital support duties including food preparation, cleaning, laundry and stock handling to keep daily operations running smoothly.

Job no: 943133

Work type: Full time

Total Indicative Remuneration: $118,024 - $190,058 p.a. - MDP2 

Temporary Full-Time, up to 30 January 2028 (Multiple Positions)

About the Role: 

An exciting opportunity is presented to work within the Northern Adelaide Local Health Network as a Medical Practitioner - General Surgery within the Division of Surgical Specialties and Anaesthetics.

The NALHN General Surgery Service Registrars will be placed across 4 units - ASU, Modbury General Surgery, Port Pirie Regional Health Service and Alice Springs Hospital.

The registrars will be offered a combination of time on 2 of these units throughout the year offering a broad exposure to emergency and elective general surgery - preferences will be asked then allocated based on suitability

This role has been designed to prepare suitable candidates for application to general surgery training through exposure to a high volume of common general surgery presentations and operations

Selected candidates will be expected to participate in research and quality improvement whilst employed in the role as well as undertaking other courses and appropriate activities to further their surgical career goals. Opportunities for teaching opportunities, research publications and higher degrees can be discussed and will be supported.

Whilst on the General Surgery unit the registrar will be responsible for supporting their senior registrar in the day to day management of both elective and emergency inpatients, interacting with allied health, supervising junior doctors, assisting in theatres and operating under direct supervision

Whilst on ASU the registrar is responsible, under the supervision of the rostered general surgical registrar, fellow and consultant for the assessment and initial management of acute surgical patients referred by the emergency department or general practitioners

On ASU registrars work a week on-off roster to provide 7 day a week continuous cover to ED and to enable the 4 hour rule of admission to function.

When visiting Port Pirie Regional Health Service you will be responsible for low acuity day surgery, outpatients, and limited scope emergency work.

Candidates rotating to Alice Springs Hospital, as a General Surgery registrar, will contribute to the delivery of elective and emergency general surgery under supervision by senior registrars and consultants, whilst experiencing the unique opportunities that Alice Springs Hospital has to offer.

The peri-operative work up, booking of cases and timely communication to senior staff is a key responsibility in this role

Monthly dedicated ASU Registrar teaching is offered by fellows and consultants.

To be eligible for this position, you must [minimum qualification requirements from Role Description]

As per the SA Health Salaried Medical Officers Enterprise Agreement 2025, the total term of employment with SA Health will be 3 years. Rotations following the initial 12 month allocation as Medical Practitioner will be determined in line with your training and SA Health's requirements. This may include transfer to other SA Health locations to perform work appropriate to classification, skills and capabilities.

To be eligible for this position, you must hold a Bachelor of Medicine; Bachelor of Surgery (MBBS) or equivalent and Registrable with the Medical Board of Australia as a Medical Practitioner with General Registration

The Total Indicative Remuneration figure is calculated taking into account base salary, leave loading and superannuation as well as managerial allowances, professional development or any other allowances where appropriate.

About You: 

In this role you will have strong interpersonal and communication skills which will enable you to successfully problem solve, resolve conflicts and negotiate, including the ability to engage in difficult conversations, whilst building and maintaining relationships. An ability to effectively manage multiple, diverse and competing priorities and demonstrated resilience within a stressful and complex environment is essential to this role.

You will be joining a dynamic and expanding Local Health Network that is committed to delivering contemporary, innovative and high-quality health services within modern facilities.

This is an excellent opportunity to contribute to a passionate, highly driven, dedicated and progressive team.

About Adelaide: 

Adelaide is consistently recognised as a city that artfully combines its compact charm and world-class cuisine with picturesque nature escapes. Ranked one of the worlds "Most Liveable Cities" and "Most Beautiful Cities", Adelaide provides something for everyone combining a wonderful mix of nature with nearby beaches, rolling hills and wildlife and culinary delights with fine dining restaurants, award-winning cafes, bustling food markets and booming boutique bars. Events like the LIV Golf, SANTOS Tour Down Under, Adelaide Fringe and the Adelaide Cabaret Festival add extra appeal to living here. 

About Us: 

The Northern Adelaide Local Health Network (NALHN) is a leading provider of public healthcare services in South Australia, and one of the largest employers in northern Adelaide. 

NALHN serves over 400,000 people in northern Adelaide with a comprehensive range of high-quality healthcare services, including emergency, surgical, obstetric, neonatal, paediatric, oncology, geriatric, palliative care and rehabilitation, and mental health care, as well as primary health care services with a focus on community health promotion and chronic disease management. 

With a commitment for ongoing upgrades to our facilities and the introduction of new services, our priority is delivering exceptional health and wellbeing services that enhance the quality of life for our community. 

With over 7,000 employees, NALHN emphasises quality care and a supportive work environment guided by respect, integrity, and accountability. Our core values foster excellence, innovation, and equitable health outcomes. 

At NALHN Everyone Has a Story, Everyone Matters, Everyone Contributes and Everyone Grows. 

Our Local Health Network Sites and Services: 

NALHN provides a range of hospital (inpatient), outpatient, community and home-based services across multiple sites in Adelaide's north and north-eastern suburbs, including Aboriginal health, mental health, and GP services. 

Lyell McEwin Hospital - the major hospital in northern Adelaide for emergency care, complex and multi-day surgery, medicine, obstetric, paediatrics and outpatient services. 

Modbury Hospital - a general hospital with emergency care, elective surgery, medicine, outpatient and sub-acute services, rehabilitation, geriatric and palliative care.

About the Role:

The Northern Adelaide Geriatric Service at Modbury Hospital is looking for a Senior Occupational Therapist to join a dedicated multidisciplinary team committed to delivering high-quality, person-centred care for older adults across Adelaide's northern metropolitan region. This is a full-time, short-term contract opportunity through to 2 May 2027.

Your Role in Geriatric Care

Working within the Northern Adelaide Local Health Network (NALHN), you will provide specialist occupational therapy assessment and intervention for complex geriatric presentations across inpatient and community-based settings. Your core responsibilities will include:

Conducting comprehensive functional, cognitive, and home assessments to support safe discharge planning and community reintegration

Delivering evidence-informed interventions focused on maintaining and restoring independence in older adults

Providing clinical supervision and professional support to junior OT staff and students

Collaborating with the broader multidisciplinary team - including medical, nursing, and allied health colleagues - to coordinate goal-directed care plans

What You'll Bring

Current AHPRA registration as an Occupational Therapist

Demonstrated experience in geriatric, aged care, or acute-subacute hospital settings

Strong skills in functional and cognitive assessment, including standardised tools relevant to older adult populations

Full Job Description
About the Business
Pacific Automotive Holdings Pty Ltd, trading as SIXT Car Rental, is a leading vehicle rental business operating from Caringbah, New South Wales. As part of the internationally recognised SIXT network, the business provides short-term and long-term vehicle rental solutions to private individuals, corporate clients, government organisations, and insurance customers. The branch manages a diverse fleet of passenger vehicles, SUVs, commercial vehicles, and specialty vehicles while delivering high standards of customer service, operational efficiency, and vehicle availability.
Operating within the highly competitive vehicle rental industry, the business coordinates vehicle acquisitions, fleet utilisation, maintenance scheduling, customer bookings, vehicle leasing, logistics, and asset management. Maintaining an efficient and well-managed fleet is critical to ensuring customer satisfaction, maximising vehicle utilisation, controlling operational costs, and supporting the continued growth of the business.
Due to increasing customer demand and ongoing fleet expansion, Pacific Automotive Holdings Pty Ltd is seeking to appoint a dedicated Fleet Manager to oversee the day-to-day management of its vehicle fleet and rental operations.

About the Role
The Fleet Manager is responsible for organising and controlling the buying, leasing, maintenance, utilisation, and operational management of the company's rental vehicle fleet. The role involves coordinating vehicle availability, customer bookings, fleet maintenance, supplier relationships, operational reporting, regulatory compliance, and customer service to ensure efficient business operations.
The successful applicant will possess strong organisational, leadership, communication, and problem-solving skills together with the ability to manage multiple operational priorities within a busy vehicle rental environment.

Key Responsibilities
The successful applicant will be responsible for:
•	Organising and coordinating the purchase, leasing, disposal, maintenance, and utilisation of rental vehicles to ensure optimal fleet performance.
•	Planning and coordinating vehicle servicing, repairs, inspections, registrations, and maintenance schedules to maximise vehicle availability.
•	Liaising with customers to determine vehicle rental requirements, provide advice regarding suitable vehicle types, rental rates, insurance obligations, and resolving customer enquiries and complaints.
•	Receiving vehicle bookings and coordinating vehicle allocation to ensure efficient utilisation of fleet resources.
•	Arranging vehicle collection, delivery, transfers, and logistics between customers, branches, workshops, and service providers.
•	Monitoring fleet availability, utilisation rates, maintenance costs, fuel usage, and operational performance.
•	Maintaining fleet records, operational documentation, maintenance histories, rental agreements, and preparing operational reports for management.
•	Coordinating relationships with external suppliers including repairers, maintenance providers, insurers, registration authorities, and transport contractors.
•	Ensuring compliance with workplace health and safety (WHS) legislation, road transport regulations, vehicle safety requirements, and company operational policies.
•	Developing and implementing procedures that improve fleet efficiency, customer satisfaction, operational performance, and cost control.
•	Supervising operational staff involved in fleet coordination and vehicle preparation while providing ongoing guidance and support.

Requirements
Australian Citizens and Permanent Residents are encouraged to apply.
Applicants should possess:
•	AQF Associate Degree, Advanced Diploma or Diploma in Business, Logistics, Automotive Management, Transport Management, Fleet Management, or a related discipline;
OR
•	At least three years of relevant work experience may substitute for formal qualifications.
Applicants should also demonstrate:
•	Experience managing vehicle fleets, rental operations, transport services, or automotive operations.
•	Strong knowledge of vehicle maintenance scheduling, fleet utilisation, and operational planning.
•	Excellent organisational and communication skills.
•	Strong customer service and stakeholder management capability.
•	Ability to prepare operational reports and maintain accurate fleet records.
•	Experience coordinating vehicle servicing, registrations, repairs, and compliance requirements.
•	Proficiency with Microsoft Office and fleet management software.
•	Knowledge of workplace health and safety legislation and vehicle compliance requirements.
•	Current Australian Driver Licence (preferred).

Work Conditions
•	Full-time, ongoing position.
•	Work location: 60–62 Captain Cook Drive, Caringbah NSW 2229.
•	Competitive salary of AUD $80,000 – $90,000 per annum plus superannuation.
•	Opportunity to work within one of Australia's leading vehicle rental businesses.
•	Professional working environment with ongoing career development opportunities.
Note: Preference will be given to suitably qualified Australian Citizens and Permanent Residents.

Northern Adelaide Local Health Network - Modbury Hospital - MODBURY SA 5092

Salary: $94,997 - $110,052 p.a. plus Superannuation and Salary Sacrifice benefits - AHP2

Ongoing Full-Time

About the Role:

Modbury Hospital's Palliative Care team is looking for a skilled Occupational Therapist to join them on a part-time basis through to 8 January 2027. If you bring a genuine commitment to end-of-life care and want to make a meaningful difference for patients and families across Adelaide's northern suburbs, this is a role worth reading about.

What You'll Be Doing

Working within the Northern Adelaide Local Health Network (NALHN) at Modbury Hospital, you will deliver evidence-informed occupational therapy assessment and intervention for patients receiving palliative care. Your day-to-day will include:

Conducting functional assessments and developing individualised goal-directed care plans in collaboration with patients, carers, and the multidisciplinary team

Providing equipment prescription, home modification advice, and carer education to support safe and dignified care at home or in the inpatient setting

Contributing to discharge planning and coordinating with community services to ensure continuity of care

Participating in team meetings, clinical supervision, and quality improvement activities within the palliative care unit

What You'll Bring

Degree in Occupational Therapy and current AHPRA registration

Experience in palliative care, aged care, or complex chronic illness settings

Confidence in functional assessment, equipment prescription, and goal-setting with patients nearing end of life

Strong communication skills across multidisciplinary teams and with families navigating difficult conversations

Alignment with SA Health's commitment to person-centred, culturally respectful care

Ability to manage a varied caseload independently at an AHP2 level within NALHN's clinical frameworks

To be eligible for this position, you must have an Appropriate Degree or equivalent qualification which entitles registration as an Occupational Therapist with the Occupational Therapy Board of Australia

About You:

This is an excellent opportunity to contribute to a passionate, highly driven, dedicated and progressive team.

About Us:

The Northern Adelaide Local Health Network (NALHN) is a leading provider of public healthcare services in South Australia, and one of the largest employers in northern Adelaide. 

NALHN serves over 400,000 people in northern Adelaide with a comprehensive range of high-quality healthcare services, including emergency, surgical, obstetric, neonatal, paediatric, oncology, geriatric, palliative care and rehabilitation, and mental health care, as well as primary health care services with a focus on community health promotion and chronic disease management.

With a commitment for ongoing upgrades to our facilities and the introduction of new services, our priority is delivering exceptional health and wellbeing services that enhance the quality of life for our community.

Our 300-plus Allied Health professionals play an integral role in multidisciplinary teams delivering outstanding care to patients across our acute, subacute and hospital avoidance services.

At NALHN Everyone Has a Story, Everyone Matters, Everyone Contributes and Everyone Grows.

At NALHN, we have a strong commitment to providing a clinically interesting professional experience, with structured and supportive education and professional development, and career progression pathways.

Some feedback from current employees about working as Allied Health Professionals in NALHN includes:

"My favourite part about working in NALHN is the close working relationships we have across Allied Health to optimise patient care."

"I feel like I'm part of a growing and developing service."

"I love the great team dynamic and the culture of learning and support."

Our Local Health Network Sites and Services:

NALHN provides a range of hospital (inpatient), outpatient, community and home-based services across multiple sites in Adelaide's north and north-eastern suburbs, including Aboriginal health, mental health, and GP services.

Lyell McEwin Hospital - the major hospital in northern Adelaide for emergency care, complex and multi-day surgery, medicine, obstetric, paediatrics and outpatient services.

Modbury Hospital - a general hospital with emergency care, elective surgery, medicine, outpatient and sub-acute services, rehabilitation, geriatric and palliative care.

Mental Health Services - adult and older persons mental health services and statewide forensic mental health services, across hospital and community settings.

Watto Purrunna Aboriginal Primary Health Care Services - provides culturally responsive primary healthcare services for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people in-hospital and across four community sites.

Primary Health Care Services - including GP Plus sites at Elizabeth, Modbury and Gilles Plains.

The position is responsible for the assessment, diagnosis and management of a broad range of dermatological disorders and contributes to the delivery of high-quality, evidence-based and patient-centred care.

The appointee will participate in departmental clinical and educational meetings, support the supervision and training of medical students, junior medical officers and dermatology trainees, and contribute to the ongoing development of specialist dermatology services in accordance with the mission, values and strategic objectives of St Vincent's Health Australia.

Personal integrity and demonstrated commitment to the Philosophy, Mission and Values of Mary Aikenhead Ministries and St Vincent's Health Australia.

Fellowship of the Australasian College of Dermatologists (FACD) and specialist registration with the Medical Board of Australia.

Demonstrated expertise in the provision of high-quality specialist dermatology services across inpatient, outpatient and consultation settings.

Demonstrated expertise and subspecialty interest in Contact Dermatitis, Procedural Dermatology and Immunodermatology, including the use of biologic agents, targeted therapies and other advanced systemic treatments.

Demonstrated ability to work effectively within multidisciplinary teams and provide specialist consultation services to referring clinicians and affiliated hospitals.

Demonstrated commitment to teaching, supervision and mentoring of dermatology trainees, junior medical officers, medical students and other health professionals.

Lismore Base Hospital & Richmond Network

Apply now to work at Lismore Base Hospital and its network sites as an Unaccredited Trainee in General Surgery for the 2027 clinical year, commencing 1 February 2027. The successful applicants will gain valuable experience in our hospitals in the beautiful Northern NSW LHD - Richmond Network, working under the guidance of highly experienced specialist surgeons and registrars on placement to Lismore on The SET Program. 

Trainees at Lismore Base Hospital gain experience in a broad range of surgery specialties including, general, orthopaedics, urology, vascular, ENT and facio-maxillary surgery. The mix will depend on your allocated terms throughout the year. 

LBH supports the education and career progression of its Junior Medical Officers by:

Education: Formal JMO teaching in Lismore includes weekly surgical teaching, monthly Grand Rounds (Whole Hospital), and Friday's surgical education sessions and M&M meetings. We also work closely with the University Centre for Rural Health (UCRH) who offer valuable teaching and simulations for medical officers in training. 

Career Progression: Following your unaccredited training year, trainees accepted onto The SET Program are able to complete placements at Lismore Base Hospital for periods ranging from 6 to 24 months. 

Where you'll be working
Lismore Base Hospital (LBH) is the recognised Trauma Centre for the North Coast Region and is linked with the local helicopter retrieval service.
The hospital is an acute regional referral hospital of 280 beds on the Far North Coast of NSW, serving a population of approximately 170,000 people on the Far North Coast of NSW and has a busy Emergency Department (40,000 presentations annually), ICU and Coronary Care Unit, as well as Surgery (general, orthopaedic and speciality surgery), Paediatrics, Mental Health, and Obstetrics and Gynaecology.

The Lismore Base Hospital theatres ward comprises of eight operating theatres, two endoscopy theatres and three recovery areas and both Ballina District Hospital and Casino & District Memorial Hospital have one theatre each.

LBH is an affiliated teaching hospital for medical students from the University of Sydney, University of Wollongong, University of Western Sydney and Bond University. The hospital has a strong commitment to teaching and support for its Junior Medical Officers.

Our region encompasses World Heritage listed rainforests and the pristine beaches of Evans Head, Ballina, Lennox Head and Byron Bay. This area is blessed by year-round sun, a tropical climate and a short winter. From lush hinterland villages, to Mount Warning, national parks, and sparkling beaches, the region is full of natural wonders and vibrant destinations all within a short drive from Lismore. 

For more information about working with us in the Northern NSW Local Health District, please visit this website - https:--nnswlhd.health.nsw.gov.au-careers-and-training-medical-recruitment 

What you'll be doing
 

The primary purpose of the Unaccredited Trainee in General Surgery is to provide safe and high quality care, assess and manage, under supervision, general surgical patients. The trainee needs to be aware of their limitations and work in a collegiate and collaborate manner. 
 

Decision making and supervision will be at the appropriate level according to the trainee's skills, knowledge and experience. The medical officer will be expected to adopt a progressively more independent approach to patient management according to their experience, under the guidance of and at the discretion of the appropriate Attending Medical Officer (AMO). All patients managed within the hospitals of the health service are under the direct care of a specialist medical practitioner. All decisions regarding their care are to be clearly communicated with the specialist responsible for that care. 
 

The position supports pre-requisites for future training positions with the Royal Australian College of Surgeons. 

 

 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 

 

Qualifications and experience commensurate with the Essential Requirements for the role (please address these in your response)

Demonstrated ability to work independently in a supervised environment.

Demonstrated ability to work effectively as part of a multi-disciplinary team with an understanding of the roles of the doctor and other members of the healthcare team.

Demonstrated high level written and verbal communication skills and ability to communicate effectively and respectfully with patients, family members and other members of the health care team.

Demonstrated good organisational and time management skills and ability to manage competing priorities in a complex environment.

Demonstrated commitment to quality improvement, patient safety and risk management.

Evidence of continuing professional development and commitment to self-education and commitment to participating in training and development opportunities to further develop skills and knowledge in the area of General Surgery.

Emergency Medicine Trainee - Stage 1
Lismore Base Hospital & Richmond Network

An exciting opportunity is available at Lismore Base Hospital for an Emergency Medicine Trainee (Stage 1) for the 2027 Clinical Year, commencing 1 February 2027, at the Lismore Base Hospital and its peripheral sites (Ballina and Casino Hospitals). The successful applicants will gain valuable experience in our hospital in the beautiful Northern NSW LHD - Richmond Network, working under the guidance of highly experienced senior clinicians as part of the Australasian College of Emergency Medicine's (ACEM) training program.

Accreditation: Lismore Base Hospital (Richmond Network) is accredited for 36 months of training as a Trainee Stage 1-3, 6 months as Trainee Stage 4 (Lismore ED), and 3 months as Trainee Stage 4 (non-ED Medical Education).

Education: We offer weekly paid protected education sessions facilitated by Dr Martin Duffy (ACEM Educator of the Year 2021), including simulation, clinical skills, case reviews, radiology, and paediatrics. Additional structured programs are offered to trainees preparing for ACEM primary and fellowship exams. LBH also supports trainees with funding external education activities including Alfred Health Emergency Procedures Course and ACEM Diploma of Pre Hospital and Retrieval Medicine. 

Where you'll be working
Lismore Base Hospital (LBH) is the recognised Trauma Centre for the North Coast Region and is linked with the local helicopter retrieval service. The Lismore Base Hospital (LBH) Emergency Department (ED) sees over 41,000 adult and paediatric presentations per year and is a regional trauma centre. The hospital is an acute referral hospital of 280 beds on the Far North Coast of NSW, serving a population of approximately 170,000 people on the Far North Coast of NSW and has a busy Emergency Department (55 beds-treatment spaces), 12 bed ICU and 6 bed Coronary Care Unit.

LBH is an affiliated teaching hospital for medical students from the University of Sydney, University of Wollongong, University of Western Sydney, University of Newcastle, Bond University, University of Queensland and Griffith University. The hospital has a strong commitment to teaching and support for its Junior Medical Officers.

Our region encompasses World Heritage listed rainforests and the pristine beaches of Evans Head, Ballina, Lennox Head and Byron Bay. This area is blessed by year-round sun, a tropical climate and a short winter. From lush hinterland villages, to Mount Warning, national parks, and sparkling beaches, the region is full of natural wonders and vibrant destinations all within a short drive from Lismore.

What you'll be doing
 

The primary purpose of a Trainee - Stage 1 in Emergency Medicine is to provide safe and high-quality care, assess and manage, under supervision, patients presenting to the Emergency Department (ED) and admitted to inpatient wards when rotating to inpatient specialities. The trainee needs to be aware of their limitations and work in a collegiate and collaborate manner. 
 
Decision making and supervision will be at the appropriate level according to the trainee's skills, knowledge and experience. The medical officer will be expected to adopt a progressively more independent approach to patient management according to their experience, under the guidance of and at the discretion of the appropriate Attending Medical Officer (AMO). All patients managed within the hospitals of the health service are under the direct care of a specialist medical practitioner. All decisions regarding their care are to be clearly communicated with the specialist responsible for that care. 
 
The position supports meeting the requirements for Stage 1 training with the Australasian College for Emergency Medicine (ACEM).

 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 

 

Qualifications and experience commensurate with the Essential Requirements for the role.

Demonstrated ability to work independently in a supervised environment.

Demonstrated ability to work effectively as part of a multi-disciplinary team with an understanding of the roles of the doctor and other members of the healthcare team.

Demonstrated high level written and verbal communication skills and ability to communicate effectively and respectfully with patients, family members and other members of the health care team.

Demonstrated good organisational and time management skills and ability to manage competing priorities in a complex environment.

Demonstrated commitment to quality improvement, patient safety and risk management.

Evidence of continuing professional development and commitment to self-education.

1x Emergency Term (Base Hospital - Lismore or Grafton)

1x Emergency Term (Peripheral Hospital - Ballina or Casino)

LBH supports the education and career progression of its Junior Medical Officers by:

Education: Lismore ED offers weekly education sessions including simulation, clinical skills, case reviews, and buddy shifts with FACEM. SRMOs are supported by EMET Lismore Hub providing access to multiple workshops including paediatric emergencies, procedural skills, ultrasound and airway management. The Anaesthetics Department is an ANZCA accredited training site which offers weekly teaching for its JMOs including formal training, teleconferenced tutorials and monthly simulation sessions held at the simulation centre at UCRH or in theatre.

Career Progression: Following your SRMO year, Lismore Base Hospital offers Intensive Care Training, or Emergency Medicine Training with opportunities to undertake 24 months accredited time across training stages 1 to 3, and training stage 4 at LBH ED, plus opportunities to rotate to ACEM accredited terms in Retrieval, Anaesthetics, ICU, Medical Education and Ultrasound. For JMOs accepted onto Anaesthetics Training Programs, we also receive rotational medical officers on the QARTS and John Hunter Hospital training programs. 

Where you'll be working
Lismore Base Hospital (LBH) is the recognised Trauma Centre for the North Coast Region and is linked with the local helicopter retrieval service.

The hospital is an acute regional referral hospital of 280 beds on the Far North Coast of NSW, serving a population of approximately 170,000 people on the Far North Coast of NSW and has a busy 32 bed Emergency Department (40,000 presentations annually), ICU (9 beds) and Coronary Care Unit, as well as Surgery (general, orthopaedic and speciality surgery) with 8 theatres, 2 endoscopy theatres and 3 recovery areas, Paediatrics, Mental Health, and Obstetrics and Gynaecology.

LBH ED also supports Richmond Network hospitals including Ballina District Hospital (18,000 presentations per annum) and Casino Memorial District Hospital (14,000 presentations per annum), and Multipurpose Centres located at Kyogle, Nimbin, Urbenville and Bonalbo. 

Grafton Base Hospital is a rural community hospital providing a wide range of accessible healthcare to the public. 

LBH is an affiliated teaching hospital for medical students from the University of Sydney, University of Wollongong, University of Western Sydney and Bond University. The hospital has a strong commitment to teaching and support for its Junior Medical Officers.

Our region encompasses World Heritage listed rainforests and the pristine beaches of Evans Head, Ballina, Lennox Head and Byron Bay. This area is blessed by year-round sun, a tropical climate and a short winter. From lush hinterland villages to Mount Warning, national parks, and sparkling beaches, the region is full of natural wonders and vibrant destinations all within a short drive from Lismore.

What you'll be doing
 

The primary purpose of the Senior Resident Medical Officer (SRMO) in Critical Care is to provide clinical care, under appropriate supervision, to patients requiring emergency, intensive care, anaesthetic or medical services in a complex clinical environment. This position will provide experience in a critical care environment and have responsibilities and opportunities for autonomous practice commensurate with the level of experience of the incumbent. 
 
Decision making and supervision will be at the appropriate level according to the trainee's skills, knowledge andexperience. All patients managed within the hospitals of the health service are under the direct care of aspecialist medical practitioner. All decisions regarding their care are to be clearly communicated with the specialistresponsible for that care.

The position supports meeting prerequisites for future training with the Australasian College of Emergency Medicine, the College of Intensive Care Medicine and the Australian and New Zealand College of Anaesthetists.
 

 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 

 

Qualifications and experience commensurate with the Essential Requirements for the role (please address these in your response)

Demonstrated ability to work independently in a supervised environment.

Demonstrated ability to work effectively as part of a multi-disciplinary team with an understanding of the roles of the doctor and other members of the healthcare team.

Demonstrated high level written and verbal communication skills and ability to communicate effectively and respectfully with patients, family members and other members of the health care team.

Good organisational and time management skills and ability to manage competing priorities in a complex environment.

Demonstrated commitment to quality improvement, patient safety and risk management.

Evidence of continuing professional development and commitment to self-education, training and development opportunities to further develop skills and knowledge in the area of Critical Care.
